text_fidelity_a: Pussan Toys for 6+ Year Old Boys Car, Amphibious Remote Control Car, 2.4 GHz RC Stunt Car Toys 4WD Off-Road Trucks, Birthday Gift for 6-12 Kids Boys Girls, Beach and Water Toys for Children This is a fun 4wd car to drive.  It runs pretty fast on the 6 volt NiCd battery.  It is nearly impossible to roll it over and get it stuck as it just flips over and keeps on going.  Battery life is good (20 to 30 mins).  Controller is a bit small for adult hands but fits my 12 year old granddaughter hands very well.  The car is not DIgitally controlled (its all on or all off- no proportional steering or throttle), but it is able to spin around while staying in place (think tank or dozer like and you get the idea).  Have not had a chance to run it in the water yet as it has been real dry here the last couple weeks.  I tested it on a mowed lawn and gravel driveway and it will handle these surfaces ok.  The plastic tires are getting a little chewed up from the gravel so do be aware that a constant gravel use will probably wear out the tires.  Also tried it on wood and carpet and it runs great on those surfaces.  It comes with a handy phillips screwdriver to take out the 4 (YES 4!) battery cover screws.  I'm guessing so many screws to help keep the battery dry when running in water.  Didn't try out the charging cord as the USB cords are nothing more than a trickle charger and take too long.  I used my B6 V2 chargerer and the battery comes out a little under spec (typical).  Remote takes 2 AA batteries.  Car is fun but there is no suspension and hard plastic tires make for a very stiff drive.  I normally run off road rock crawlers in a dry creek bed so this car really isn't designed for that type of use, but for smooth surface running this is a good fun choice.
text_fidelity_b: Pussan Toys for 6+ Year Old Boys Car, Amphibious Remote Control Car, 2.4 GHz RC Stunt Car Toys 4WD Off-Road Trucks, Birthday Gift for 6-12 Kids Boys Girls, Beach and Water Toys for Children

TAOZI&LIZHI Christmas Puzzles for Adults 1000 Pieces, Christmas Harbour Holiday Cheer, Xmas Vacation, Jigsaw Puzzle Gifts for Women Men Families, Nightmare Before Christmas Decorations(27×20in) I rediscovered my love of puzzles when COVID hit, and I was doing a traveling job, so I was stuck in a corporate apartment in a shut down city knowing NO ONE. When I wasn't at work, I was cooking, doing movie marathons, and puzzles.

I love the puzzles that require a true strategy, rather than the obvious "let's get the edges first" or "oh, all the purple stuff is in this corner". This puzzle begged for a solid strategy, because the drawing is complicated, and there's some duplication. You can't take anything for granted with this jumble! As well, the poster that comes with it does NOT include the added glow-in-the-dark ink pressed on top, so you have a guide, but it's also got surprising additions to trip you up.

My last pic shows how vivid the glow-in-the-dark ink is. I took this at dusk, with a lot of light still spilling in, and those teeth are GREEN.

All in all, this puzzle is a head scratcher and a definite win.

Klutz Painted Rocks Craft Kit Multicolor, 10.5" Length x 0.75" Width x 8.5" Height This craft kit comes with a book on rock painting, eight acrylic paints, one paint brush, four pairs of self-adhesive googly eyes, and one rock. The kit is for ages 6 and up. The 40 page book comes with instructions on how to use the acrylic paints and included 28 step-by-step instructions for creating various paintings, from animals and flowers to various people, foods, and more. The book also contained pictures of other rock painting ideas but left it to the reader to figure out the steps needed to get the finished product. Most of these were pretty obvious and were similar to previous step-by-step projects.

The acrylic paints are white, black, blue, yellow, red, orange, green, and purple. Some of the designs required mixing these colors to make a new color, and adults may need to help younger kids with this. The paints had something in them to slow the drying time a little (so more like 30 minutes for dry to the touch rather than just a few minutes more typical for acrylic). This allowed for more time to make changes or mixing color on the rock.

The value in this kit is mainly the book as you only get one rock (thankfully...they're easy enough to get locally) and the painting supplies aren't going to go very far (maybe 10-20 rocks?). Still, this kit is enough to see if this is something your child enjoys. I painted the rock in the photo using the book instructions, but modifying the design to fit the rock.

text_fidelity_a: Petit Collage Animal Friends Magnetic Game Board with Mix & Match, Ideal for Ages 3+, Includes Mag Play Scene Treehouse Party, 74 Count This magnetic playset has 72 magnetic pieces, 2 backdrop scenes, and a box to hold the set. The set is made for ages three and up. The sturdy cardboard box has a lid that lifts up and can be set in a groove in the sides of the box so it acts like an easel. The bottom side of the lid has a magnetic backdrop of a tree house. There is a thin, magnetic backdrop in the box that you can place over this scene to transform it into a picnic scene. There are four characters: a rabbit, a bear, a fox, and a squirrel. There are various pieces for play imaginative play, from birds, bees, leaves, and flowers to furniture and food. The smaller pieces are about half an inch square, so they could be a choking hazard or easily lost if not kept attached to the backdrop or in the box. The pieces are thick enough (just over 1 cm) that they should endure play fairly well. They easy popped out of the magnetic sheets that they initially came in. The magnet strength is strong enough to hold them in place during play or travel while still easy to remove from the backdrop. Overall, if your child likes imaginative play, this can be a fun set. My niece enjoys making up stories playing with these pieces.

text_fidelity_a:
Sew Mini Gardens (Klutz Craft Kit) The Klutz kits are hit and miss for us, but this one was a hit. Now, that said, like a lot of the Klutz kits, this is a difficult one for children, and will require a very hands on adult helper.

The designs are very nice, and the instructions are good throughout if you have Google or sewing knowledge. It's not that it's going to be terribly difficult to figure out how to sew necessarily, but some of the designs are reasonably complex. I'm not a sewer, but I could figure it out, and instruct my little ones. There are a lot of steps to some of them, and the dexterity needed means that this is going to be one for the older children almost exclusively - they'll need some "advanced" skills like maintaining an even stitch pattern that is not too widely spaced or narrow, figuring out what "whip-stitching" is without it being explained thoroughly, and so forth. Because the designs are all fairly small, you can make one, then save the rest for later, and the kit will see use for many crafting sessions.

I'm very impressed by the finished product as well. Overall, a fun and educational experience for the little ones and for myself as well.
text_fidelity_b: Sew Mini Gardens (Klutz Craft Kit)

Hot Wheels Star Wars Carships Death Star Revolution Race Track Set The box says this toy is for 5 and up. It's one of those toys that will have appeal to a great variety of ages. I could easily see any fan of Star Wars having fun playing with this thing, no matter what age, even teens and adults. I've enjoyed it myself. IF my children grow tired of it, I think I'll just claim it for my own.

The great thing about this toy is that it looks cool, too. It makes a great display toy. I prefer having toys hidden when not in use, but this one even looks great on a dresser(or something similar).

You do have to assemble it, but it didn't take me long. I gave an inward sigh of impatience when I dumped all the pieces out of the box, but it really wasn't that bad. It only took a few minutes to get it all together. Stickers have to be applied, too. Apply them carefully, because they're difficult to move without tearing.

It's loud! Conversation of any kind isn't the best idea while it's on, unless you're willing to yell to be heard. It takes 4 D batteries, and those are NOT included. We don't typically keep D batteries around, so we bought some before opening the package.

It has a place to hold up to 6 cars when not in use. It takes some practice to get the car to crash into the middle, so it's not something that will happen automatically for most.

Overall, this is a really cool toy. All my children have enjoyed it, and I have, too.

text_fidelity_a:
QOGELY Home Decor Blaster Building Kits This is not a “puzzle”, but a “model”. I can only assume that they do not have a word for “model” in Chinese. Because Chinese companies always list items like this is a “puzzle” though it’s really not.

This model is made of wood. It shows to have 47 pieces. There are 3 boards with the cutout pieces. You’ll want to use caution when removing the pieces from the boards so that you do not break them. You remove the pieces from the boards as you go. The pieces are numbered on the instruction sheet, but not on the boards. So if you remove them all at 1st, it will make it very difficult to put the model together. I highly recommend you have either a razor blade or thin sharp knife available to help remove the pieces. If you simply use your fingers, you could easily break a piece.

I must admit that I am not a person who likes to build models. So it took me about an hour and ½ to put this together. It turned out okay, but not as perfect as the pictures. The shingles do not fit perfectly. Nonetheless I think it looks okay.

Also, when you get to pieces 12, 13, 14 and 15 which is part of instruction number 5… Those 4 pieces make a little platform. The way the instruction show it on instruction number 9, that platform sits inside section B. But if you place it there, then the top shingle portion sits on top of the platform and is not sturdy. If you don’t put that platform there, then the top piece see fits in to the bottom piece a which makes it sturdy. Then I use that platform as a base on the bottom to place the temple on top of. Written on that platform is “Temple of Serenity”. So because of that, I think it should go on the bottom is a base anyway. But of course you can do it anyway you want to.

An optional string of LED lights is included. Two AA batteries are required and not included.

As a bonus, there is also a small “Ellie House” which is 24 pieces.

This model is made in China and being sold by a Chinese company on Amazon. At the current price of 30 bucks I think it is a bit expensive, but it is a unique and interesting item. Also, it comes in a nice cardboard box, which makes it easy for wrapping if you’re giving it as a gift.
text_fidelity_b: QOGELY Home Decor Blaster Building Kits

text_fidelity_a: Halloween Lights- 24 pcs Halloween LED Necklace Bracelets Pumpkin Ghost Pirate Spider Eyeball Necklace Halloween Party Favor Light up Flashing Decoration Trick Treats Gift Bag Fillers for Women Men Family Pack There are 24 different Halloween themed pieces in the box, ranging from pumpkins, to ghosts, to pirate ships, to spiders, to skulls.  The necklaces have a simple snap clasp at the end, and the bracelets have two different size settings.  The lights have three different colors including red, green, and blue.  There are three different setting to the lights with how they flash.  When first turned on, all three of the colors work great.  All the red, green and blue lights work at first.  But after about 10 minutes, the blue light starts to fade, then the green light starts to fade, until only the red light is working.  If turned off and left to sit and rest for a while, then all three light begin to light up and work again, but eventually again only the red light will remain lit.  This happened with all of the necklaces and bracelets in the box.  So as long as the lights are not needed to stay on for long periods of time, they are nice.  If needed for longer periods, two bracelets or necklaces or one of each could be used to alternate between them to give each one a rest by turning it off to refresh the colors.  So if handing these out for Halloween treats, I would recommend giving kids two in order to compensate for the lights not working all the time.

text_fidelity_a:
SHASHIBO Shape Shifting Box - Award-Winning, Patented Fidget Cube w/ 36 Rare Earth Magnets - Transforms Into Over 70 Shapes, Gift Box, Download Fun in Motion Toys Mobile App (Black & White, 4 Pack) This is much more fun than I thought it would be.

It's easy to get started, but gets really tough to figure out all the shapes when you know that there are *allegedly* over 70 shapes to make with it.

Right out of the box, it looks a lot like a weird little cube. It's maybe a little smaller than a standard Rubik's cube for comparison. But this cube is more complex, even though it doesn't have as many permutations as Rubik's.

The printed portions have nice patterns (on this cube, there are three different patterns depending on the configuration). Once you start playing with it, you can't put it down.

Even though it says in the instructions that you might have trouble getting it back to its cubic form, it's really not that hard and it also seems to be the default shape that you will keep returning to again and again, even when you're obsessing about discovering another shape.

I'd recommend this for anyone who enjoys puzzles and mind games. Even if they don't, this might get them thinking more spatially. There's a certain thrill of finding a new shape that you never knew was there. And the satisfying *click* sound when you get one. So far, I'm nowhere close to the 70+ that the box mentions. I can make a couple dozen, but then it's back to a cube. It's very weird even to try to duplicate the same shape you just had only a few seconds ago.

Nothing negative about this that I could find except maybe if the cube starts to wear out after a ton of usage. It seems to be made with vinyl stickers that will hopefully last a long time, though.

And one word of warning: I can imagine certain personality types getting frustrated with this and tearing it to a pile of tiny little plastic pyramids.

Overall, this gets a solid 5-stars. I'll probably get at least one more of these since they can be combined to create even more variations.
text_fidelity_b: SHASHIBO Shape Shifting Box - Award-Winning, Patented Fidget Cube w/ 36 Rare Earth Magnets - Transforms Into Over 70 Shapes, Gift Box, Download Fun in Motion Toys Mobile App (Black & White, 4 Pack)

text_fidelity_a:
Feleph Jungle Trees Building Blocks Bricks with 2 Base Plates (10 Inches for Each), Forest Garden Plants Flowers Bushes Animals Kit, Botanical Parts Scenery Toys Compatible with Major Brands LEGO would never make something like this. Sure, you can take their stuff and make anything with them, but too many of their kits make a definitive something. This is a definitive nothing, but a nothing that can entertain far beyond what a lot of different "somethings" can do.

LEGO is a toy, and this is often something that they remember to a fault. Here is a LEGO competitor, with bricks that are compatible, that remembers that it's not always a toy that kids want. They want an experience of playing, and that's what this Forest Garden kit gives them. Is it a dinosaur jungle? Is it a very nice tropical garden? Are the characters running from that alligator, or picnicing i the woods? With this, more than with any LEGO kit I've ever reviewed, there is a limitless number of possibilities.

There are no instructions with this kit, which is somewhat bothersome for the finnicky children who need a "right" way to put them together, but the playscape this provides is so unique that I can't give it less than 5 stars.
text_fidelity_b: Feleph Jungle Trees Building Blocks Bricks with 2 Base Plates (10 Inches for Each), Forest Garden Plants Flowers Bushes Animals Kit, Botanical Parts Scenery Toys Compatible with Major Brands

text_fidelity_a: Hanatora Air 2S,Mavic Air 2 Wall & Car Charger Compatible with DJI Air 2S,Mavic Air Battery, 5 in 1 Rapid Multi Parallel Charging Hub Drone Accessories I tried both the charging and the discharging function. It seems that it functions as claimed. The max charging rate is 2.2 amps per battery. Discharge is at a lower rate of about 1.5 amps. Rates taper off neat the end of the cycle. The charger won't start to charge a battery that is at or above 90% full. It will not start to charge a battery that is too hot. The instructions imply that balancing is applied at the end of the charge or discharge which is very important for the health of LiPo batteries. Taking the unit apart, I found the internal construction to be reasonable with well-sized and quality components. Soldering looks good and much better than I had expected. I will stick with the DJI charger and hub for charging my batteries as I am usually not desparate for lots of charged batteries quickly. However, I really like being able to discharge the batteries for storage so that will be my main use for the charger. I would say this is a good purchase for maintaining our expensive batteries.
text_fidelity_b: Hanatora Air 2S,Mavic Air 2 Wall & Car Charger Compatible with DJI Air 2S,Mavic Air Battery, 5 in 1 Rapid Multi Parallel Charging Hub Drone Accessories

text_fidelity_a: NATURALIFE 1byone Professional Bubble Machine with High Output, Automatic Blowing Mechanism for Outdoor or Indoor Use Started to buy one of the more expensive models but noticed this one didn't have any mention of foaming issues so decided for the price to give it a try. WOW! This thing is great! Thousands of bubbles most just under tennis ball size but some smaller. If you use the Gazillion Bubble solution you get beautiful iridescent bubbles that drift a long way before breaking. It works best and the bubble sdrift farther if you can get it up off the ground. A breeze helps too. I set it on the top step of a 3-step ladder and that was perfect. This machine is a bubble solution hog but it couldn't be any less and produce this volume of bubbles. Seems to run maybe 20 minutes or so on a fill and you get about 4 fills from a bottle of the 2 liter Gazillion Bubbles solution. It can make a but of a mess on the ground under the machine so be sure to place it somewhere that doesn't matter or is easy to clean. I didn't find the machine all that difficult to clean after using but you have to have a little patience. Hold it upside down and use the garden hose on low flow to wash out the solution tray being careful not to wet the motor or switch.. We ran this off and on over the 3 day July 4th weekend and it ran perfectly. Kids and adults both were amazed. If you want a bubble machine and don't want to spend a lot of money get this one.
text_fidelity_b: NATURALIFE 1byone Professional Bubble Machine with High Output, Automatic Blowing Mechanism for Outdoor or Indoor Use

1. It feels “ok well” made and feels like its probably worth around 50-60$ in techology and material.
2. The screen resolution looks good
3. It says there is over 36000+ game on it.

Now lets get into the negative aspects:

1. Graphics: This emulator is VERY weak / has low processing power which makes “heavier” games basically unplayable/unenjoyable. (Framerate Drop, Audio Stretching, Gamespeed dropping)
2. Audio: The included audio speaker sounds like it is broken on my device and Mono only, which is alright, the issue is the games have been so compressed that most audio just sounds terrible.
3. Price: This device is too expensive for how it performs, it should be aroun 70-80$ max.

Conclusion:

I would Not recommend this emulator - if you are looking for a handheld gaming experience, you may want to look into a nintendo Switch or a Steam Deck.

text_fidelity_a:
Traxxas 6608 LaTrax Alias Quad-Rotor Ready-to-Fly Helicopter, Assorted Colors The Alias is potentially a great example of the new generation of quadcopters with electronic flight control boards that provide six axis stabilization. When their transmitter control levers are properly trimmed at the beginning of each flight they will hover very stably and are easy to fly even for a beginner.

Unfortunately, LaTrax and Traxxas (LaTrax makes the product and Traxxas provides all customer support) released the Alias before they found a good quality motor that works properly with the Alias. Since the Alias uses four motors and is inoperable if any one of the motors fails this is a major problem.

My Alias flew great for the first two days, but then it became very unstable and flew unpredictably. After only the the sixth or eighth flight one of the motors failed and the Alias would not fly at all.

Traxxas told me the Alias does fly unpredictably when one of its motors is weakening and getting ready to fail. They said they would send me a free replacement motor, but so far it has not arrived. Looking at other Amazon reviews, and on the internet, I see that many other people have also had very early motor failures. I strongly recommend people should not buy the Alias until LaTrax and Traxxas have figured out the early motor failure problem, presumably by finding a better motor.

Update: January 14, 2014

After two initial days of use before one of the motors broke, I have been unable to fly my new Alias for two and a half weeks now. Traxxas keeps saying they will send me a new motor as soon as the most recent batch they received "gets through quality control". I fear I have wasted $150 to buy the Alias.

Update January 20, 2014

After three weeks Traxxas finally sent me a replacement motor ....drum roll.....however, they sent the wrong motor! Traxxas checked their records, agreed they had sent the wrong motor, and promised to send the correct motor. I am pleased they are trying to provide good customer service, but I am now in my fourth week without being able to fly my otherwise excellent Alias after one of its motors broke on the second day after I opened it at Christmas.
text_fidelity_b: Traxxas 6608 LaTrax Alias Quad-Rotor Ready-to-Fly Helicopter, Assorted Colors

text_fidelity_a:
So Slime DIY - Mini Slime Caddy Our library has monthly slime making labs that my children enjoy. It's created a greater interest in the world of slime for them and it's something fun for us to enjoy when boredom strikes, especially in the late evening/night hours. This kit was enjoyed by all of us. It comes with a little caddy(and a removeable tray) to hold the supplies. Inside, there are two containers for making the slime, stickers for decorating the containers, 4 packs of slime powder, 4 packs of decoration(glitter and small shapes), and 2 little toys(ours isn't what's shown...star and cloud here). To make the slime, all the maker has to do is add the slime powder and any glitter/shapes they want, then fill to the line with water, put the top on, *hold* it on well, and then shake it until it's the right consistency. We had to shake longer than the directions said, but it still doesn't take long and it's super easy.

Just to note, the glitter still gets everywhere. It doesn't stick to the slime like I thought it would. While playing with the slime, it came off on our hands a great deal. I found glitter everywhere afterwards, despite us trying to be careful with it. It was on us, the table, the floor, the couches. My husband wasn't even here when we made it, nor did he play with it, but he even ended up with glitter on his face the next day. So, keep that in mind if you dislike glitter as much as I do. Too, my children didn't like the shapes in the slime, saying it poked their hands. It comes off the slime, too. Otherwise, we've enjoyed it!

text_fidelity_a:
Globe 540 Piece 3D Puzzle Ball I love geography and travel, and putting this together is both fun in a puzzle sort of way and great for reminiscing about past travels and dreaming about places yet to be seen in person. It's really cool - even cooler that it comes with a stand and you have a globe of your own afterward.

It is very up to date - it includes S. Sudan. And a warning to independence haters: Kosovo is shown as its own country. It is quite small and not labeled, but it has its own color.

We did the first half (the bottom) in the first night, but used the numbered backs as a guide as shown on the instruction sheet. It was fun, but left something to be desired. I wished they didn't have the numbers, and thought they would be impossible to ignore. After this, this was going to be the first Ravensburger puzzle I would have given less than five stars.

BUT the second night we finished it, but without the numbers. Turns out they were easy to ignore, and this allowed it to be what it should have been all along.

It might be overwhelming to not look at the numbers at first, but I suggest you do it that way. I suspect you still will have it done in 3-4 nights (assuming a few hours each night - it is addicting).

The pieces are plenty durable for snapping together, but many pieces are alike, so you could conceivably put the whole thing together as a sphere, but have it still be wrong. Anyone with any sense of geography would be able to catch a mistake like that. And when in doubt, the backs are numbered.

And when you're done, you have a nice little globe, textured to show it was a puzzle, and with a reasonably good looking stand. Very neat.
text_fidelity_b: Globe 540 Piece 3D Puzzle Ball

Snap Circuits Classic SC-300 Electronics Exploration Kit | Over 300 Projects | Full Color Manual Parts | STEM Educational Toy for Kids 8+ 2.3 x 13.6 x 19.3 inches I got this kit for my 10 year old. We had been experimenting with kit electric motors, magnets and radios and everything ended up mixed in a box that he liked to play with, so there was interest in this type of toy.

The parts of this kit snap together on a clear plastic grid. The instruction book is a black and white center stapled pamphlet that can be challenging to decipher for builds that are more complex. My son liked building the simple circuit that included the motor with the fan. Many of the advanced plans are very similar.

The kit seems durable but not indestructable. My kids can be pretty rough on things so they have been using this kit with my supervision.

For most kids under 10, this is not the type of toy that they can play with on their own. I have my son use this toy at the dining room table. We check to make sure that all of the parts get back in their place when we are done.

This is an educational toy. My experience is that early exposure to learning experiences like this can shape interests later on in life.

I would have liked to have seen a description of what the various modules do to the electricity to make the magic happen.

If you have any specific questions please leave a comment and I'll try to get back to you as soon as I can.

text_fidelity_a:
Monopoly Empire Game "Monopoly Empire" is like a simplified version of the traditional game of Monopoly. The colors and layout of the board are very similar to the traditional game, but each has a famous logo, such as Hasbro or EA Sports, instead of street names. The object of the game is to add tiles with various brands to your Times Square type "billboard tower" before the other players. The more brands you add to your billboard, the more money you get when passing Go, which allows you to buy more brands. The game tokens are representative of the brands in the game, such as a bottle of Coca-Cola and an Xbox controller. The board is a bit smaller than the traditional board, because it doesn't have railroads.

The game is easy to learn, in part because of an excellent, full-color instruction guide that includes a very clear diagram of how to set up the board. The way the items are priced make it easy to pay for purchased tiles. Although the game is lacking the excitement and strategy of trading properties and building houses as in the original version of Monopoly, it is good for a quick game. It would be easy for kids to learn and play. The game is most fun when it's a close race between the players to complete their towers. If one player takes a large, early lead, it's hard for the other person to come from behind.

Note: The logoed tiles have various sizes, which is part of the game. However, the sometimes the positioning of the stickers with the logo make it confusing to put them into the tower correctly.

All in all, this is a good game that is easy to play and goes by quickly.
text_fidelity_b: Monopoly Empire Game
